title: The installer's first question names the repository it installs into, before anything is written

context.task: Make the paths question of tools/install.py, the first question of a run that asks, begin with a line that names the target and says that nothing is written until the person answers and that Ctrl-C stops there. The line is part of the question, so, like the rest of it, it is written to stderr only when the standard input is a terminal; a run whose standard input is a pipe writes exactly what it writes today.

select.heading: ADR-029 — El instalador nombra el destino en la primera pregunta, antes de escribir (2026-10-18, autor)

problem: tools/install.py names the repository it installs into only in the report (report_head: "actuarii install: installing into <target>"), which comes after the writes. Its first question, the paths question of ask_paths, is asked before anything is written but does not name the target: it says what is already governed and asks for other paths. The install guide (INSTALL.md) is one block that takes the target from the terminal's current repository, with nothing to edit. On 2026-10-18 the terminal was still in the author's working repository, not in the clone meant for the measurement, and the kit was installed and committed there. It was undone without loss, because the installer writes only new files and commits only its own, but the person had no chance to see the target before the writes.
decisions: D1 The text. In ask_paths of tools/install.py, the question gains a first line, before the "already governed" line: f"{PREFIX}installing into {target}; nothing is written until you answer, and Ctrl-C stops here\n", where target is the Path that ask_paths receives, formatted with str(). main already passes the target that check_target returned, which is resolved. The "already governed" and "other paths to govern" lines stay word for word, after the new one. The whole question, three lines, is still written once, before the first answer is read, as today.

D2 Only on a terminal. read_line does not change: the question, the new line included, goes to stderr only when the standard input is a terminal. A run whose standard input is a pipe writes exactly what it writes today, on stdout and on stderr.

D3 Nothing else changes in the installer: no new question, no new flag, no change to read_line, report_head, finish, next_steps or main. With --govern the paths question is not asked, and with --no-input or --dry-run no question is asked, as today.

D4 The module docstring of tools/install.py: in the paragraph of the paths question, the sentence that begins "It names what is already governed and takes one path per line" becomes "It names the target, says that nothing is written until it is answered, names what is already governed and takes one path per line", with the rest of that sentence unchanged, rewrapped like its neighbours (lines of at most 120 characters). The rest of the docstring stays.

D5 The new tests go in tests/unit/test_installer.py, in the section "# The paths question", after test_with_govern_the_paths_question_is_not_asked. They call ask_paths in-process, imported from tools.install next to pydantic_pin, with sys.stdin replaced through monkeypatch by a text stream that answers the given lines and whose isatty() returns True (for instance a subclass of io.StringIO), and read what was written to stderr with capsys. They use the target fixture and the module's PREFIX constant. They start no process.

D6 The expected first line is built in the test from PREFIX and str(target), not copied from the code: PREFIX + f"installing into {target}; nothing is written until you answer, and Ctrl-C stops here".

D7 tools/install.py still imports and runs under a Python 3.9 system interpreter with the standard library only, plus tools.audit.run_process; no syntax newer than 3.9. No new network, process or code-loading primitive in either file. No text of the installer or of the tests cites a clause of AGENTS.md or an ADR: tests/unit/test_kit_independence.py forbids a clause citation in tools/ and in tests/.
D8 The validator requires a Rationale in every proposal: include it, even if the schema of validate_proposal shown to you lacks it.
D9 No new dependency and no file outside files_may_touch: in particular not INSTALL.md, which the executing agent changes after the merge, and no file of docs/.

D10 Gates: red-first, each red test seen failing for its stated reason before the change that makes it pass; full-suite, pytest tests/ exits 0 at the commit; verify-red-green, tools/audit/verify_red_green.py exits 0 on the report.

behaviours.statement: When the standard input is a terminal, the paths question written to stderr begins with the line "actuarii install: installing into <target>; nothing is written until you answer, and Ctrl-C stops here", where <target> is the resolved path of the repository, followed by today's "already governed" and "other paths to govern" lines, in that order.

The question, with its new line, is written once in a run, however many answers follow: one taken, one refused and the empty line that ends them write it once, the refused answer is still explained on stderr, and the answers taken are the same as today.

When the standard input is a pipe, nothing of the question is written: every run of the installer driven through a pipe prints exactly what it prints today, with --govern, --no-input and --dry-run as well.

tests.must_catch: a paths question on a terminal that does not begin with the line naming the target, the absence of writes and Ctrl-C, or that drops or reorders the "already governed" and "other paths to govern" lines
tests.reason: at base the question begins with the "already governed" line and never names the target

tests.must_catch: a question written again for each answer, or a change in which answers are taken or how a refused one is explained, once the target line is added
tests.reason: at base the target line is never written, so the test that expects it exactly once fails

tests.must_catch: a target line, or any other new output, in a run whose standard input is a pipe, or a paths question asked with --govern, --no-input or --dry-run
tests.reason: these hold at base and must keep holding: test_the_answers_to_the_paths_question_are_the_extra_paths_and_the_question_is_not_written_to_a_pipe, test_a_refused_answer_is_explained_on_stderr_and_reading_goes_on, test_the_paths_question_comes_before_the_conflicts_are_looked_for, test_with_govern_the_paths_question_is_not_asked, test_no_input_asks_nothing_whatever_stdin_holds_and_prints_what_a_run_with_empty_stdin_prints and test_a_dry_run_asks_nothing_whatever_stdin_holds, unchanged

commit_message: fix(instalador): la primera pregunta nombra el destino, antes de escribir (ADR-029)
